name: Shoe
overview: Scripture uses the imagery of shoes to convey holiness, humility, and covenantal relationships. God commanded Moses to remove his shoes on holy ground, illustrating reverence before the divine presence (Exodus 3:5; Joshua 5:15). Shoes also symbolize commitment and refusal within family duties, as seen when a brother-in-law’s shoe is loosed to signify declining levirate marriage (Deuteronomy 25:9). Furthermore, the Israelites' shoes not wearing out during their wilderness journey reflects God's sustaining provision (Deuteronomy 29:5), while the metaphor of shoes made of iron and brass signifies enduring strength (Deuteronomy 33:25). The shoelatchet represents careful stewardship and integrity, as Abraham refused to take even the smallest part of spoils (Genesis 14:23).
